items.title: Over 100 Israeli settlers burn Palestinian homes, clash with troops in West Bank
items.summary: JALUD, West Bank: More than 100 Israeli settlers have attacked a village in the occupied West Bank, preventing a Palestinian family from returning home and clashing with troops, witnesses said. Around ten minutes after they reached the homes, a group of over 100 settlers descended, witnesses said. The settlers set the homes on fire, blocked access roads, and hurled rocks toward Israeli officers, three of whom were injured, the Israeli military said in a statement.

items.title: Tun M admitted to IJN for routine treatment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad was admitted to the National Heart Institute (IJN) yesterday for routine treatment. His press secretary Sufi Yusoff said Dr Mahathir was fatigued and had not been getting enough rest following the death of his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali, on Monday. Dr Mahathir was earlier reported to have been admitted to IJN today.

items.title: Penang draws 285,400 medical tourists, RM601.8m revenue in first half of 2026
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 30 — Penang received about 285,400 medical tourists and generated RM601.8 million in medical tourism revenue in the first six months of this year, state tourism and creative economy committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said today. Citing Malaysia Healthcare Travel Council (MHTC) data, he said the figures demonstrated the sector’s significant scale and Penang’s continued importance to Malaysia’s medical tourism industry. He said Penang received about 520,000 medical tourists and generated RM1.14 billion in revenue last year.

items.title: Former Felda DG charged with cheating board over Jalan Semarak land transfer
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — A former director-general (DG) of the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) was charged at the Sessions Court here today with deceiving the authority’s board of directors in connection with a power of attorney used to transfer the ownership of 16 parcels of its land at Jalan Semarak in 2014. Faizoull, in his capacity as Felda DG, is accused of deceiving the board by concealing a power of attorney dated June 3, 2014, granted Synergy Promenade Sdn Bhd authority to transfer ownership of the 16 parcels of land involved in the proposed Felda Lot Development Project at Jalan Semarak. The act induced the board of directors to agree to the power of attorney, resulting in the transfer of ownership of the said Felda land to Synergy Promenade KLVC Sdn Bhd and Synergy Promenade Sdn Bhd, when the Board would not have done so had it not been deceived.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia rebounds at opening on bargain hunting
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's key index rebounded to open higher on Wednesday as bargain hunting emerged after recent losses, despite negative cues from Wall Street. At 9.10am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) recovered 4.34 points, or 0.26 per cent, to 1,648.30 from Tuesday's close of 1,643.96. The index opened 2.53 points higher at 1,646.49.

items.title: Hamas commander among seven killed in Israeli strikes across Gaza
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Gaza's civil defence agency said that Israeli fire on Tuesday killed at least seven people, including a Hamas commander, confirming an earlier report from the Israeli military. The agency, which operates as a rescue force under Hamas authority, said that Izz al-Din al Beik was killed in an Israeli strike west of Gaza City, together with another man. The Israeli military confirmed Beik's role as commander of Hamas's northern Gaza brigade, and said he had directed Hamas operatives to carry out attacks against Israeli troops and civilians.

items.title: Former Felda chief pleads not guilty to cheating over land transfer
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Felda director-general Datuk Faizoull Ahmad pleaded not guilty today to a charge of cheating the agency's board of directors into approving a power of attorney that resulted in the transfer of ownership of 16 Felda land parcels in 2014. According to the charge, Faizoull, who was Felda director-general at the time, had dishonestly concealed from the board that a power of attorney dated June 3, 2014, had granted Synergy Promenade Sdn Bhd the authority to transfer ownership of Felda-owned land involved in the proposed development of Felda lots at Jalan Semarak. He was alleged to have dishonestly induced the Felda board of directors to approve the power of attorney, resulting in ownership of the 16 parcels being transferred to Synergy Promenade KLVC Sdn Bhd and Synergy Promenade Sdn Bhd.

items.title: Syed Saddiq remembers Siti Hasmah through love, legacy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Muar member of parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman has chosen to remember the late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali by celebrating her life, love and contributions to the country rather than through tears alone. Syed Saddiq said Dr Siti Hasmah's passing was not merely the loss of a prominent figure, but also the end of an extraordinary love story between two people who complemented each other throughout their lives. "A life companion.

items.title: VS Industry poised for re-rating as earnings recover, orders improve
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: VS Industry Bhd could see a re-rating as improving orders, higher plant utilisation and customer diversification support an earnings recovery, said UOB Kay Hian Research. The firm said the electronics manufacturing services provider's established manufacturing capabilities, technical expertise and spare capacity positioned it to secure new programmes as customers diversify their manufacturing operations. VS Industry returned to the black in the fourth quarter ended July 31, 2026 (Q4 FY26), posting a core net profit of RM21.4 million against a core net loss of RM32.9 million in the preceding quarter and RM18.4 million a year earlier.

items.title: California officially recognises Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha as state holidays
items.summary: HAMILTON: The US state of California has officially recognised Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha, the two major Islamic holidays, under a new law signed by Governor Gavin Newsom. Assembly Bill 2017, signed into law on Sunday, adds the holidays to the official state holiday calendar, according to Anadolu Agency. "The designation of Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha as state holidays is a civil calendar determination that acknowledges their cultural significance to California communities," the law stated.

items.title: Woman found dead with head and neck injuries at Tawau plantation, husband arrested
items.summary: TAWAU, Sept 30 — A 37-year-old Indonesian woman was reportedly found dead with injuries at a plantation workers’ quarters in Felda Umas, Jalan Kalabakan, on Monday, with police arresting her husband in connection with the case. According to Sinar Harian , Tawau police chief ACP Rosdi Mat Jusoh said the woman, who worked at the plantation, was found unconscious following an incident at about 4.55pm and was pronounced dead at the scene at about 8.16pm. Police reportedly arrested the victim’s 38-year-old Indonesian husband, who had also suffered an injury to his neck and is receiving treatment at Tawau Hospital.

items.title: Police detain lorry driver after fatal Bagan Lalang crash
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH: A lorry driver has been detained after a motorcyclist died in a crash at Jalan Perusahaan Sungai Lokan 6, Bagan Lalang. Seberang Prai Utara district police chief, Assistant Commissioner Anuar Abdul Rahman, said the 54-year-old man was detained to facilitate investigations under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987. "Initial investigations found that the container lorry was turning left into Jalan Perusahaan Sungai Lokan 6 when the motorcyclist was travelling alongside the lorry on its left.

items.title: HI Mobility 2H FY27 earnings to gain traction on bus deliveries, ridership
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: HI Mobility Bhd's earnings are expected to remain firm in the second half of financial year 2027 (2H FY27), driven by higher commercial vehicle deliveries and stronger cross-border bus ridership during the holiday season. As at end-July, HI Mobility had an unbilled order book of RM211 million, providing earnings visibility, the firm said. The outlook follows a stronger second quarter, with HI Mobility's core net profit rising 8.7 per cent quarter-on-quarter to RM19 million, while revenue increased seven per cent to RM119.3 million.

items.title: Do you recognise this man? Bentong police seek help to find missing soldier
items.summary: In a statement yesterday, Bentong district police chief ACP Zaiham Mohd Kahar said police received a report yesterday regarding the disappearance of Muhammad Danial Asraf Azizan, 21, from his 41-year-old mother after he could not be contacted. He said Muhammad Danial was last seen at Charlie Company, 25th Battalion of the Royal Malay Regiment (RAMD) camp in Bentong. Members of the public with information on his whereabouts are urged to contact the nearest police station or the Bentong district police headquarters District Control Centre (DCC) at 09-223 1999.

items.title: Customs seizes 701 refurbished iPhones hidden in vegetable boat
items.summary: AYER KEROH: A total of 701 refurbished iPhones of various models were seized by the Royal Malaysian Customs Department in Melaka. The seized phones, including iPhone 11 to iPhone 16 Pro Max models, were estimated to be worth RM716,184 including duties and taxes. Melaka Customs director Roslan Yusoff said the phones were found by the Melaka Customs Marine and Enforcement Team during an inspection of a barter trade boat at Port Klang jetty, Selangor, at 4.30am on July 23.

items.title: Ringgit opens lower against major currencies, US dollar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened lower against major currencies including the US dollar on Wednesday as weaker United States consumer data weighed on investor sentiment and reduced risk appetite in the foreign exchange market. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam said the Conference Board's confidence index fell 81.9 points in September, the lowest level since April 2014. At the opening, the ringgit traded lower against a basket of major currencies.

items.title: Police arrest 74 Chinese, Vietnamese, Taiwanese nationals in KL scam call centre bust
items.summary: Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the simultaneous raids on eight residential premises were conducted in collaboration with the Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID). “Checks found that all eight premises were believed to be linked to activities promoting online gambling, ‘love scams’ and non-existent investment scams, besides being used as hostels or accommodation for call centre operators,” he said in a statement yesterday. M. Kumar said the raiding team also seized various electronic devices believed to have been used for the criminal activities, including computers, laptops, modems and mobile phones of various brands.

items.title: 440 detained as French teens clash with police in school protest crackdown
items.summary: PARIS: French teenagers on Tuesday set fire to rubbish bins and threw projectiles at police who responded with batons and tear gas, with hundreds detained across the country over the blockades and protests demanding better conditions at schools. Since last week, students have staged protests outside hundreds of schools over grievances including timetables, class sizes and a shortage of teachers as well as overheated classrooms during this year's heatwaves. The protests started in the Ile-de-France region around Paris but have now spread to other cities nationwide.

items.title: KLVC scandal: Former Felda senior exec to face fraud charges today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — The former senior officer of the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda), who was previously investigated in connection with the misappropriation of the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project, will be charged in the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court today. Meanwhile, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) stated that it has obtained the green light to charge the former senior Felda officer. The KLVC investigation is part of seven investigation papers involving Felda and Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC), comprising six new investigation papers and one previous investigation.

items.title: US Supreme Court lifts limits on third-country deportations
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US Supreme Court on Tuesday lifted restrictions on the deportations of immigrants to countries that are not their own, while agreeing to hear the issue on its merits in December. The conservative-dominated high court granted an emergency request by the Trump administration to suspend a lower court ruling that restricted, but did not outright ban, so-called "third-country removals." The lower court ruling "created substantial logistical problems" with removals, he said.

items.title: Guan Eng wants foreign workers excluded from minimum wage hike
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng wants the government to exclude foreign workers from any increase in the minimum wage. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had said the current RM1,700 minimum wage was expected to be raised, with details to be announced when 2027 Budget is tabled. Lim said any increase should not apply to foreign workers, arguing that local employers had hired them based on previously agreed employment contracts.

items.title: Man tries to stab policeman, believed to be depressed
items.summary: KAJANG: A 54-year-old man who allegedly attacked a policeman at the Batu 9 Police Station compound on Saturday is believed to have been experiencing depression linked to family problems. Kajang district police chief, Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof, said the suspect attempted to stab the policeman during the incident at 12.10am. Earlier, media reported that a policeman narrowly escaped being stabbed by a man while opening the gate at the Batu 9 Police Station here.

items.title: Oil prices settle down 2.5pct on signs Middle East exports recovering
items.summary: HOUSTON: Oil prices settled 2.5 per cent lower on Tuesday as investors focused on signs of recovering crude exports from the Middle East, although prices headed for monthly gains on lingering concern about supply disruptions during the US-Israeli war on Iran. Brent crude futures closed down US$2.69, or 2.6 per cent, at US$102.59 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude settled down US$3.22, or 3.5 per cent, at US$89.38.

items.title: Equities end slightly lower as bond yields hold near multi-decade highs
items.summary: NEW YORK: US stocks ended the session slightly lower on Tuesday, as government bond yields continued their ascent ahead of inflation and labour market data, while investors assessed comments from Federal Reserve officials for the path of interest rates. Longer-dated US Treasury yields rose, with the 30-year bond hitting 5.62 per cent, its highest since June 2002. Williams said the US central bank has time to weigh the data before deciding when to hike interest rates again.

items.title: UM makes history as first Malaysian university to enter global Top 200
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's oldest university, Universiti Malaya (UM), has entered the global Top 200 in the Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings (WUR) 2027, rising to 194th and becoming the first Malaysian university to achieve the milestone. With 2,297 universities ranked worldwide, UM is now positioned among the top 8.5 per cent globally, while retaining its position as Malaysia's highest-ranked university in THE World University Rankings. Universiti Malaya Vice-Chancellor Datuk Seri Professor Ir Dr Noor Azuan Abu Osman said the achievement reflected the collective strength of the university and signalled a stronger Malaysian presence in global higher education.

items.title: Lapid hits Netanyahu over 'fear-mongering' attack warning ahead of election
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Israel's opposition chief early Wednesday accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of fear-mongering after he alleged that enemies may attack before Oct 27 elections. "Netanyahu ignored every warning before Oct 7 and now, 28 days before the election, he's suddenly busy fear-mongering," Lapid said. Netanyahu's office said he provided the briefing alongside military leaders to Lapid soon after the opposition leader has requested it in response to Netanyahu's remarks.

items.title: Indonesia vows tougher fight against fires, transboundary haze [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Indonesia has pledged to step up operations to contain forest and land fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan to address the threat of transboundary haze, which has also affected Malaysia. "Indonesia has implemented various measures to prevent and tackle fires and haze, particularly in Sumatra and Kalimantan. Meanwhile, Iman said Indonesia was tightening monitoring and enforcement against illegal forest and land-burning.

items.title: Universiti Malaya becomes first Malaysian university to break into Times Higher Education Top 200
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Universiti Malaya (UM) has become the first Malaysian university to break into the global Top 200 of the Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings, securing 194th place in the 2027 edition. UM vice-chancellor Datuk Seri Profesor Dr Noor Azuan Abu Osman said the milestone reflected the collective strength of the university community and represented a stronger Malaysian presence in the global higher education landscape. THE World University Rankings is a research-intensive university ranking system that assesses institutional performance across five pillars, namely teaching, research environment, research quality, industry and international outlook.

items.title: What is UMP? How Malaysia’s new free medicine delivery service works and how to apply
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — The government yesterday launched the subsidised Ubat Melalui Pos (Postal Service for Medicines) programme, which it said would benefit more than 85,000 patients. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil waves the Jalur Gemilang to flag off a Pos Malaysia delivery rider, accompanied by Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching and Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad, during the launch of the Medicine Delivery via Post (UMP) Funding Initiative at the Communications Ministry in Putrajaya, September 29, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel What is UMP?

items.title: Odes to KL city, underground subcultures, and ‘Tbaka Daghat’: How Malaysian zine makers are documenting the country
items.summary: Malay Mail got in touch with several of these zine makers to learn more about how they are doing their part in archiving local culture; this includes views from a local underground music enthusiast, a Kelantan-based independent book publisher and an architecture lecturer turned archiver. Archiving 30 years’ worth of Malaysian underground music Abdul Mutalib Jaamat, a zinemaker and the founder of local underground music blog Altar Aksara. As there is little documentation about these underground bands, 42-year-old Abdul Mutalib Jaamat, a zinemaker and the founder of the underground blog “Altar Aksara”, is on a mission to archive all releases by local underground bands, specifically their vinyl releases, in a book series.

items.title: North Korea denies South Korea's claim it was behind DMZ mine blasts
items.summary: SEOUL: Kim Jong Un's powerful sister denied a South Korean claim that North Korea was apparently behind landmine blasts last week that injured three soldiers, state media reported Wednesday. After carrying out an investigation into the incident, the South Korean Defence Ministry said it concluded that North Korean mines were "highly suspected" of causing the two explosions. "This is a clear violation of the armistice agreement, and since North Korea bears responsibility, we will take corresponding measures," South Korean Defence Minister Kang Shin-chul said Tuesday.

items.title: Malaysians gather to pay their last respects
items.summary: MEMBERS of the public gathered at the National Cemetery in Presint 20 here yesterday to pay their last respects to Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali. He said when serving the family in Langkawi, he had the opportunity to interact closely with Dr Siti Hasmah, whom he described as warm and motherly. [[nid:1544292]] "She shared many views and offered advice like a mother would, especially about daily life," he said at the cemetery yesterday.

items.title: Fadhlina: CCTV coverage beefed up
items.summary: THE Education Ministry is expanding closed-circuit television (CCTV) coverage to 333 boarding schools this year with an additional RM5 million allocation. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said 300 MySTEP warden assistants had also been deployed to student hostels since April to boost student safety and curb bullying. "I understand parents' anxiety whenever a bullying incident occurs.

items.title: Trump backs AI industry pledge to police itself
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Tuesday said the tech executives gathered at the White House to discuss regulating AI had signed a "morally binding" commitment to build adequate safeguards on the fast-moving technology. "They're going to police themselves," Trump said after the meeting that gathered the top leaders in artificial intelligence, including Nvidia's Jensen Huang, OpenAI's Greg Brockman and Anthropic's Dario Amodei. Meta boss Mark Zuckerberg said the accord aims to assure customers that AI technology "works in the way that we intend."

items.title: Pentagon picks Boeing for new US Navy contract for air strike weapons
items.summary: NEW YORK: The Pentagon has chosen Boeing to build the Navy's next-generation fighter jets in a contract valued at US$20 billion, US officials announced Tuesday. In March 2025, Trump announced that the Air Force chose Boeing to build a new stealth fighter. We are ready and able to build multiple concurrent future combat aircraft franchise programs," said Steve Parker, head of Boeing Defence, Space & Security.

items.title: Google appeals against EU order to share data
items.summary: BRUSSELS: Google LLC said yesterday it has appealed a European Union (EU) decision requiring it to share data with other search engines and open up its Android system to rival artificial intelligence (AI) services, citing privacy concerns. "We're appealing decisions that will force us to share people's private search history without sufficient anonymisation and weaken vital security protections on Android," said Google's senior director for competition, Oliver Bethell. In July, the European Commission said Google must start sharing search data from January 2027 to "rebalance the playing field".

items.title: China visit opens opportunities to expand strategic cooperation, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said his recent visit to China provided an avenue for Malaysia to explore and expand strategic cooperation, underpinned by the increasingly close diplomatic ties between the two countries. The post also featured a two-minute-and-57-second video highlighting the Prime Minister's working visit to China, set to the popular Mandarin-language song "Tian Xia", sung by Jason Zhang. Anwar made the three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou from Sept 22 at the invitation of his Chinese counterpart, Li Qiang.

items.title: Anwar echoes Sultan Nazrin's call for shura and adab
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has echoed Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah's call for the principles of shura (consultation) and adab (civility and proper conduct) to guide Muslims, particularly in navigating differences of opinion and competing ideas. Anwar said Sultan Nazrin's address at the National Council for Islamic Religious Affairs (MKI) meeting yesterday was profound and insightful and should be widely understood and shared with the public. Anwar said Sultan Nazrin's emphasis on adab was equally significant, as the concept extended beyond conduct to encompass education, learning, consultation and interpersonal relations.

items.title: SAM demands answers after president barred from entering Sarawak
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Sahabat Alam Malaysia (SAM) has condemned the denial of entry into Sarawak of its president Meenakshi Raman. SAM honorary secretary Mageswari Sangaralingam said Meenakshi had received no letter, notice or prior indication that she was prohibited from entering Sarawak. Mageswari said Meenakshi had been allowed to enter Sarawak as recently as 2024.

items.title: After Finance Ministry says no duty due on K8 cargo, Maritime Network asks Customs dept to put ruling on record
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Maritime Network Sdn Bhd is seeking a written explanation from the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM) following a meeting with the Ministry of Finance (MOF) over the handling of Atlanta crude discharged at Tanjung Langsat under a K8 declaration. At the September 25 discussion, chaired by MOF Tax Division Under-Secretary Datuk John Patrick Antonysamy and attended by JKDM officers, the chair said no duty was due on the cargo as presented. Maritime has also separately raised questions about another Atlanta crude cargo carried by MT Marlin Santorini.

items.title: Sarawak vaccinates 3,579 dogs, distributes 2,281 oral rabies vaccine baits in latest drive
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 29 — A total of 3,579 dogs have been vaccinated through Sarawak’s recent field rabies vaccination efforts this year, alongside the distribution of 2,281 oral rabies vaccine (ORV) baits, said Premier Datuk Patinggi Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg. He said the ORV programme provided an important last-mile approach to reaching free-roaming dogs that were difficult to capture and vaccinate through conventional methods. Abang Johari said Sarawak continued to strengthen its rabies prevention and control measures through vaccination, surveillance, enforcement, public awareness and collaboration with its partners.

items.title: Home minister: Government resolving persistent refugee problem according to rule of law
items.summary: He said that a total of 5,000 Myanmar refugees have been finalised to undergo a voluntary and phased repatriation programme back to their country of origin, based on the Myanmar government’s agreement to accept them and the individuals’ consent to return voluntarily. “Today, a total of 1,476 individuals began the First Phase of repatriation, based on the list submitted by the Myanmar Government through an official Diplomatic Note. This resolution was also achieved through diplomatic approaches and direct negotiations with the Myanmar Government,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB seen leaving palace after nearly three-hour audience with Tuanku Muhriz
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 29 —Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim concluded an audience with the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, at Istana Hinggap here after spending nearly three hours at the palace. Earlier, vehicles carrying Undang Luak Sungai Ujong Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari and Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid were also seen entering the palace grounds. The affected Exco members are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Datuk Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah.

items.title: PM Anwar: Malaysian government to continue talks with Myanmar on refugee status
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the Malaysian government will continue engaging with Myanmar to find an amicable solution to the long-standing issue of refugees. He said the issue, which has remained unresolved for decades, had become more complicated as the number of refugees increased, including through negotiations on their possible return. He said without resolve and negotiations, it may lead to protests.

items.title: PM Anwar: Professional expertise must go beyond specialisation to bring Malaysia forward
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today called on Malaysia’s professional community to move beyond narrow specialisation and work across disciplines. He said expertise alone was insufficient to drive the country’s progress. “What is great about professional life is that it brings together people from different disciplines, different races and different regions,” he said when launching the Professional Conference and Exhibition 2026 (PROFEX 2026) in conjunction with the Malaysia Professional Day.

items.title: PM Anwar says will ‘discuss’ transport minister’s plan to resign
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has said today he will discuss Anthony Loke’s decision step down as Transport Minister. This comes after the Prime Minister receiving Loke’s letter of resignation yesterday. Earlier today, Loke said he will stay on as transport minister until former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak begins his house arrest.

items.title: UN concerned by Malaysia returns of Myanmar migrants
items.summary: GENEVA, Sept 29 — The UN voiced worry today as Malaysia started sending thousands of Myanmar nationals back to the war-torn country, warning that conditions there would not enable “safe, dignified and sustainable returns”. Malaysia began repatriating around 1,500 Myanmar nationals today, launching the first phase of a return programme that has raised concerns from rights groups. The group is the first of 5,000 Myanmar nationals that Malaysia says have agreed to “voluntary” repatriation from detention centres.

items.title: Women’s ministry: Victims of sexual harassment need to speak up, no shame in it
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Sept 29 —The Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) is calling on students to know their boundaries, dare to say no, and seek help if they face sexual harassment or violence. We also want to teach them how to seek help when someone faces sexual harassment or violence. Lim said bullying, sexual harassment and violence require a cross-ministry approach, covering advocacy, prevention, awareness and counselling.

items.title: Heavy rain, gusty winds expected across peninsula and Sarawak until 7pm, warns MetMalaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning for several states in Peninsular Malaysia and Sarawak, with thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds expected until 7pm today. In Peninsular Malaysia, the warning covers Penang, Perak and Melaka, as well as parts of five other states. In Sarawak, the warning covers Sri Aman, Betong, Sarikei (Sarikei and Maradong), Sibu (Sibu), Samarahan (Sebuyau) and Kapit (Song).

items.title: Woman found unconscious behind a building in Sabah dies
items.summary: PENAMPANG, Sept 29 — A 38-year-old local woman died after she was found unconscious on the ground behind a building in Donggongon here yesterday. Penampang police chief Supt Sammy Newton said police received a report on the incident at about 12.36pm. Those with information are urged to contact the investigating officer, Penampang police station chief Insp Ahmad Amir Fitri Ab Rahman at 016-449 2215.

items.title: DVS tests 18 dogs following rabies scare in Kedah’s Changlun
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — The Kedah Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) has collected samples from 18 dogs in Changlun, Kedah, and surrounding areas for rabies confirmatory testing as of yesterday, following an incident where a man was bitten by a stray dog in the area. Subsequently, Kedah DVS conducted an on-site investigation and carried out operations to capture stray dogs in collaboration with the Kubang Pasu Municipal Council to locate the suspected animal and assess the potential presence of the rabies virus. Kedah DVS is continuing its investigation and awaiting laboratory results to confirm the presence of rabies among dogs in Kedah,” the statement read.

items.title: Home Ministry: 1,476 Myanmar nationals leave Malaysia in first ‘voluntary’ repatriation phase
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — A total of 1,476 Myanmar nationals departed Malaysia today under the first phase of a “voluntary” repatriation programme aimed at resolving a protracted, decades-long refugee and undocumented migrant challenge, the Home Ministry (KDN) announced. The operation is being conducted by sea via two naval vessels and a hospital ship deployed by the Myanmar government, coordinated jointly by KDN, the Immigration Department of Malaysia (JIM), and relevant security agencies. KDN stated that as of Aug 15, a total of 10,388 Myanmar nationals held across Immigration detention depots nationwide have been undergoing biometric identification, immigration status assessments, and security screenings.

items.title: MACC: Ex-senior exec to be charged over RM42m UiTM Holdings loss
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — A former senior executive of a corporation will be charged in court this Thursday in connection with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigation into losses incurred by UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd, including allegations of abuse of power regarding operational expense payments to several companies totalling about RM42 million. “The arrest follows an investigation conducted by MACC regarding issues concerning losses suffered by UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd (UiTM Holdings) in 2023,” the statement read. Meanwhile, MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrest when contacted and stated that the case is being investigated under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009.

items.title: Guan Eng says foreign workers should be excluded from minimum wage hike, calls for EPF levy repeal
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 29 — DAP chairman Lim Guan Eng today called on the government to exclude foreign workers from any increase in Malaysia’s minimum wage, arguing that the move would help protect local businesses, particularly micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), from rising operating costs. While acknowledging the rationale for higher wages, Lim said the prospect of a minimum wage increase has sparked concern among local businesses already grappling with intense competition, higher compliance costs and taxes, as well as price pressures from overseas producers. According to Lim, exempting foreign workers from minimum wage increases and scrapping the EPF contribution requirement would help ease cost pressures on local businesses and safeguard the viability of approximately 1.2 million MSMEs nationwide.

items.title: Public to get live access to Sabah 40pc revenue appeal at Kota Kinabalu court
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 29 — Up to 250 members of the public will be able to follow the Court of Appeal hearing on Sabah’s constitutional 40 per cent revenue entitlement next month through a live audiovisual transmission at the Kota Kinabalu Court Complex. The arrangement will allow members of the public to watch the proceedings from the court’s conference hall while the appeal is heard inside the courtroom on Oct 29. The Court of Appeal is scheduled to hear the federal government’s appeal against the High Court’s October 17, 2025 decision in the judicial review brought by the Sabah Law Society (SLS).

items.title: Marina Mahathir: My father healthy but lonely after loss of beloved wife
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — Former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad is coping with a deep sense of loneliness following the death of his wife, Tun Dr Hasmah Mohd Ali, whom he shared more than seven decades of marriage with, according to their daughter, Datuk Marina Mahathir. Berita Harian reported that Marina said her 101-year-old father remains in good health but is grieving the loss of his lifelong companion, who died yesterday at the age of 100. He feels lonely,” Marina told reporters after visiting Dr Hasmah’s grave at Pusara Negara in Presint 20 today.

items.title: Dr M recalls shock at wife Dr Hasmah’s sudden passing despite signs of good health
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Sept 29 — Former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad has said he did not expect his wife, Tun Dr Hasmah Ali, to pass away yesterday, recalling that she had appeared to be in good health the night before. Dr Mahathir also thanked the royal family for making the journey from Pahang to offer their condolences. Dr Hasmah died at about 9.25am yesterday at the National Heart Institute.

items.title: Nanta: New Johor Bahru court complex among 11 judicial projects worth RM736m nationwide
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Sept 29 — The new Johor Bahru court complex in Kota Iskandar is among 11 judicial infrastructure projects being developed nationwide with a cumulative value of RM736 million, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said today. “The Johor Bahru court complex project was approved by the Economic Planning Unit (EPU) of the Prime Minister's Department back in 2018 under the 11th Malaysia Plan. Also present at the event was Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.

items.title: Fahmi: Only register for medicine delivery service through MoH to avoid scams on Facebook, TikTok
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — Applications for the government's medicine delivery service (UMP) should be done only through the Ministry of Health, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today as he cautioned against possible scam attempts. "I remind everyone there is no registration process other than at health clinics or Ministry of Health facilities only." Patients in Malaysia will soon be able to receive their follow-up medication delivered directly to their doorstep free of charge, following a joint funding initiative announced today by the Communications Ministry and the Health Ministry.

items.title: Health minister: Mission is to transform healthcare within 15th Parliament timeframe
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad wants the national healthcare transformation agenda, including modernising the system and improving patient service delivery, to be completed within the 15th parliamentary term. He said the Ministry of Health (MOH) faces a major challenge of not only keeping facilities ready but also ensuring healthcare delivery consistently meets the people’s needs. Dzulkefly said MOH faces increasingly complex challenges, including food safety and quality, mental health and planetary health.
